title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this 1986 'Analysis situs' draft, Grothendieck builds an axiomatic, combinatorial 'tame topology'. The data are a set 𝔐 of strata (elementary pieces) and a set 𝔉 of figures. Figures are certain sets of strata, ordered by ≤ (inclusion) and equipped with a compatibility relation. 𝔐 splits into components 𝔐_i (i∈I). Restriction F ↦ F|𝔐_i gives a map 𝔉 → ∏𝔉_i.

On p.64, axiom C4 says strata lying in disjoint components are compatible. Its consequence is that the image of 𝔉 → ∏𝔉_i contains every family with almost all F_i = ∅. The map is a bijection when I is finite. If all figures are of finite type ('t.f.', also called 'compl. finis'), then so are the 𝔉_i, and the image is exactly the families with almost all F_i = ∅.

Page 65 justifies Cor. 3 by condition 1 and a Lemma. The Lemma states that F is of finite type iff (a) every component F_i is of finite type and (b) all but finitely many F_i are empty. This is the expected statement: a finite-type object meets only finitely many connected components.

Grothendieck then fixes notation:
- π0(F) for a figure, with functorial maps π0(F) → π0(G) when F ≤ G, and transitivity.
- π0(𝔐), and a π0^d(𝔉).
He warns that π0^d(𝔉) is not the π0 of the poset (𝔉, ≤). It is a π0 that takes supports into account. More generally, for a structure 𝒞 = (𝔉, ≤, a relation on non-permutable / incompatible pairs) one should consider π0(𝒞).

He next states a strengthened axiom, C4 bis: for every family (F_i) ∈ ∏𝔉_i there is F ∈ 𝔉 with F|𝔐_i = F_i for all i. So 𝔉 → ∏𝔉_i is surjective, hence bijective. This allows 'locally finite' figures with infinitely many nonempty components.

The new section, headed 'Contrôle résiduel(?) — Support et complément', opens as follows. Take a set Φ = {H_i} ⊂ 𝔉 of figures. A figure F is disjoint from all H_i iff each stratum of F is (cf. C3). This prepares p.66. There Grothendieck defines cosupp(Φ) as the figures (or strata) disjoint from Φ, and supp(Φ) = cosupp(cosupp(Φ)). These form a Galois connection induced by the disjointness relation, with saturated ('closed') parts on both the 𝔉 side and the 𝔐 side.

Purpose of the page: set up a calculus of connected components and of supports and complements for a combinatorial model of stratified or tame spaces.
errors: No mathematical error. The machine transcription's 'b) Tous les F_i sauf un nb fini sont ≠ ∅' is inverted. The image and the logic require 'sont ∅' (all but finitely many are empty).
Gap: π0^d(𝔉) is only hinted at ('en tenant compte des Supp'). The relation in 𝒞 = (𝔉, ≤, ·) is crossed out or illegible, so the definition is not given on this page.

ideas.what: Finite-type figure iff finitely many nonempty components, each of finite type
ideas.modern_name: a quasi-compact / finite-type object has finitely many connected components

ideas.what: Axiom C4 bis: figures are freely glued from arbitrary families of component-wise figures
ideas.modern_name: coproduct decomposition / sheaf-like gluing over connected components (locally finite figures)

ideas.what: π0 of figures, functorial in F ≤ G; warning that the relevant π0 of the set of figures differs from the poset π0 and must account for supports or compatibility
ideas.modern_name: connected components of a stratified space vs. of its poset of strata/figures

ideas.what: Support and cosupport of a set of figures via disjointness, checked stratum-wise
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity (orthogonal complement) induced by the disjointness relation

missed.claim: This page is part of an unpublished axiomatic 'analysis situs' for tame or stratified spaces. Grothendieck only programmatically announced this project (Esquisse d'un programme, §5–6, 'topologie modérée'). The page itself contains only routine bookkeeping (components, π0, supports).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's own axiomatics for tame topology, which can be compared with o-minimal structures and stratified-space formalisms. The content on this page alone is not new.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine lemmas on connected components and the start of a support/cosupport Galois connection inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. Historically interesting as context, but mathematically standard.
transcription_corrections: 'b) Tous les F_i sauf un nb fini sont ≠ ∅' should read '... sont ∅'.
'π0^{!}(𝔉)' on the left is most likely the same π0^d(𝔉) as on the right (a superscript d with a struck-out mark).
Heading 'Contour résiduelle' is uncertain; it is possibly 'Contrôle résiduel' or similar. The word under '𝒞 =' also read 'contour' is likewise uncertain.
'Ceci résulte [-de C4-] cond. 1 et de (compl. fini) Lemme': the struck-out word is 'C4' and the Lemma is labeled 'Lemme' (struck or underlined) with the marginal '(compl. fini)'.
